wave: CORRECTNESS -- strip_comment was quote-unaware, so a # inside a quoted attribute value truncated the value AND, when on a block's own header/footer line, corrupted collect_block's brace-depth counter, potentially absorbing subsequent declarations into the wrong block with zero diagnostic
wave_title: Sixteenth generation this cycle, and a fourth real bug found in core/src/language/adl/mod.rs. A follow-up survey deliberately targeted this file's remaining logic after three prior real bugs there this cycle, on the reasoning that a file yielding multiple real defects is worth one more careful pass before moving elsewhere. Found a real defect in strip_comment, the shared comment-stripping helper this generation's OWN prior fix (collect_block) directly depends on for its depth computation.
priority_classification: correctness/architectural integrity -- highest category in the standing priority order. A real, silent data-corruption defect reachable via wholly ordinary ADL syntax (a quoted attribute value containing a literal #, e.g. an issue-tracker reference), with zero diagnostic, capable of both truncating a value and -- via its effect on this generation's own collect_block fix -- corrupting block-boundary detection so a subsequent declaration is silently absorbed into the wrong block.
gap_discovered_by: Delegated Explore subagent survey, explicitly scoped to core/src/language/adl/mod.rs's remaining logic (parse_relation, span tracking, dispatch matching, declared/observed reconciliation) distinct from the three already-fixed bugs, using git log to confirm exactly what had already been fixed. Its finding was independently re-verified before any change: read strip_comment's real, current implementation directly (confirmed the naive split('#') with zero quote awareness), read collect_block's real consumption of strip_comment's output for its depth computation directly (confirmed the exact corruption mechanism: a truncated header line losing its closing brace leaves depth above zero, so the loop does not terminate on that line and keeps consuming subsequent lines as if they belonged to the same block), and confirmed this session's own earlier collect_block fix (this same generation cycle) already introduced quote-aware helpers (quote_aware_tokens) elsewhere in this exact file, making strip_comment's own lack of the same discipline a real, internally-inconsistent gap rather than a hypothetical one.
key_finding: strip_comment implemented `line.split('#').next().unwrap_or_default().trim()` -- entirely unaware of `"..."` quoting, unlike unquote/quote_aware_tokens elsewhere in this same file, which already correctly treat `#` inside a quoted string as literal text. For a wholly ordinary attribute value like `description = "See issue #42 for details"`, strip_comment truncates everything from `#42` onward, discarding the value's own closing quote. When this line is ALSO a single-line block's own header/footer (e.g. `capability Foo { description = "See issue #42 for details" }`), the truncation additionally removes that line's closing `}` from the text collect_block's depth counter reads -- corrupting the counter (it stays above zero instead of reaching zero) and causing the block to silently swallow every subsequent line until something else in the file happens to rebalance the count, absorbing a wholly unrelated subsequent declaration (e.g. `capability Bar { ... }`) into the wrong block's body with zero diagnostic anywhere. Independently confirmed both symptoms (value truncation and block-boundary corruption) are real and distinct, not merely one manifestation described two ways.
verification_before_acting: Read strip_comment's real, current implementation directly, confirming the exact naive split('#') behavior.

Read collect_block's real consumption of strip_comment's output directly (the `let clean = strip_comment(raw);` binding immediately followed by `depth += clean.matches('{').count(); depth -= clean.matches('}').count();`), confirming the exact mechanism by which a truncated closing brace corrupts the depth counter and prevents block termination.

Confirmed this exact quote-unawareness is an internal inconsistency, not merely a plausible-sounding hypothetical: quote_aware_tokens (introduced by this same generation cycle's own prior collect_block fix) and unquote (pre-existing) both already handle `#`/other characters correctly inside quoted spans elsewhere in this exact file -- strip_comment simply never received the same treatment.
Checked the existing test suite for any strip_comment/#-in-quotes coverage and confirmed none exists -- only the plain #-starts-a-comment path was ever exercised.

design_decisions.question: Rewrite strip_comment from scratch, or reuse quote_aware_tokens (this generation's own earlier addition)?
design_decisions.decision: A small, purpose-built character-scan (tracking an in_quotes boolean, returning the line up to the first #-outside-quotes) rather than reusing quote_aware_tokens directly -- that helper tokenizes and DISCARDS whitespace/structure, which is the wrong shape for strip_comment's own contract (return everything up to the comment marker, preserving the line's own structure for collect_block's brace-counting and parse_assignments' own key=value splitting downstream). The two functions solve genuinely different problems (tokenize vs. truncate) even though both need the same quote-tracking primitive; duplicating that small amount of logic here is simpler and clearer than forcing one function's shape onto the other's use case.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: strip_comment no longer treats a # inside a quoted attribute value as a comment marker, closing both the direct value-truncation defect and its downstream corruption of collect_block's brace-depth counter for single-line blocks.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: Added a_hash_inside_a_quoted_attribute_value_is_never_treated_as_a_comment, reproducing the exact scenario from the report: a capability Foo with a quoted description containing a literal #, followed by a separate capability Bar, asserting BOTH that Foo's description survives intact AND that Bar is recorded as its own distinct declaration (never absorbed into Foo's body). Falsified per this session's standing discipline: backed up the file, reverted the fix to the original naive split('#'), ran the new test, confirmed it failed with the exact expected truncation (description truncated to "See issue" instead of the full quoted value), then restored the fix from backup (git diff --stat confirmed the restored file exactly matched the fix) and confirmed the test passes.
